races.name: Find Us At Fitzdares.com Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Shady Bay
runners_data.note: Won over this sort of trip on good ground and holds strong similar-going form (11/15 including three wins); Tom Ward's yard is in modest current form (1/10 over 14 days) but this horse has a clear tactical edge as the lone confirmed front-runner, and good-to-firm conditions suit.

runners_data.name: Just An Hour
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's six-year-old has consistent placed form over 10-12f on good ground and sits at the right end of the weight range; naturally prominent, likely to sit a length or two off Shady Bay and represents the most logical beneficiary if the leader ties up late.

runners_data.name: Mythological Star
runners_data.note: Daniel & Claire Kubler's three-year-old comes here just six days after their last run and jumps sharply in trip from 7-8f to 1m2f, which is a significant unknown; hold-up style will need the pace to be genuine, and their recent form (1-3-3) has been at shorter distances on good and standard ground, making trip stamina the key question.

runners_data.name: Hello Cotai
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse who has won on good ground over 10f and showed a recent win in that trip range; mapped to midfield because the rear is crowded with closers, meaning they may not get the clear late run their style demands — sim-going record is modest (5/15) by comparison with their headline form.

runners_data.name: Golden Circet
runners_data.note: Jim & Suzi Best's six-year-old has been running consistently over longer trips (12-16f) and steps back in distance here; hold-up in style with no current-form momentum (0 wins in 14 days for the yard) and a modest similar-going strike rate (1 win, 3 places from 7 runs), so needs a truly run race that this pace map does not strongly suggest.

runners_data.name: Post Rider
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer by profile, but this field cannot accommodate another horse pressing Shady Bay, so Oliver Cole's five-year-old is effectively racing out of their preferred role here; recent form has been patchy (7-3-5-8) and the STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence, though they have decent similar-going placed form (3 wins, 7 places in 15 comparable runs).

races.paceDynamic: Shady Bay is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner apprentice handicap over Windsor's flat 1m2f, and with no genuine rival to push them, they should be able to dictate on a comfortable, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground. Just An Hour and Post Rider are both naturally prominent types, but with Post Rider redistributed to midfield on the map and Just An Hour likely to settle just off Shady Bay rather than fight for the front, the early pace should be orderly rather than pressured. Golden Circet, Mythological Star, and Hello Cotai are all hold-up horses by profile, though Hello Cotai is redistributed to midfield because the field carries more genuine hold-up types than can all occupy the rear realistically. This controlled, single-paced shape on fast ground strongly favours a horse able to travel prominently and sustain their effort rather than those needing a truly run race to land a late blow — patient closers face the real risk of never seeing enough daylight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shady Bay Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Shady Bay is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a true but manageable tempo that stretches the closers on good-to-firm ground.
scenarios.body: Shady Bay dictates every yard from a handy position, and with no rival willing or able to apply sustained pressure, the race is run at a speed that suits a horse who can see it out from the front; Just An Hour, travelling just behind, is best placed of the rest to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Hold Edges Late
scenarios.trigger: If Shady Bay sets only a dawdle and the field bunches, allowing a horse sitting just off the pace to pounce in the straight.
scenarios.body: A slow early gallop compresses the field and turns the race into a short sprint home on ground that rewards a sharp, well-balanced horse; Just An Hour or Post Rider, sitting handily without expending energy early, picks up neatly inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Gets Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to exhaust the leaders and create a gap for a hold-up horse to thread through in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Mythological Star, stepping up significantly in trip but showing recent form on good ground, or Golden Circet, if their stamina carries them past tiring rivals in the final furlong; this shape depends on Shady Bay setting a stronger clip than their profile suggests, which remains the less likely outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Chaos Decides
scenarios.trigger: If traffic and positional jostling from the competing prominent types create interference and the result is settled by fortune as much as merit.
scenarios.body: Post Rider and Hello Cotai, both out of their natural role in this race shape, could benefit if the race is messy enough that positional advantage becomes irrelevant and a clear run decides matters; this scenario hinges on multiple horses failing to settle cleanly, which is unlikely in a small, well-spaced field.

watchPoints.text: Shady Bay's ability to stride clear unchallenged is the axis of this race — if Ashley Lewis has them fully settled and confident in front, the hold-up horses simply may not generate enough momentum to reach them on good-to-firm ground.

Mythological Star jumps dramatically in trip to 1m2f on only six days' rest — watch early for signs they are struggling to settle in a rear position over a distance they have never tried, as stamina failure here would be abrupt.

Post Rider and Hello Cotai are both out of their natural positional roles and carry STYLE_FIT discounts — if either apprentice jockey tries to force their horse back into a preferred early position, interference or early burning of energy is a real risk.

Just An Hour's trainer Rod Millman has sent a 6yo on an 18-day turnaround after a placed run — note whether Charlie Tucker (7lb claimer) settles them smoothly in the slipstream of Shady Bay, as that positioning call will define their finishing chance.

Good-to-firm ground at Windsor over 1m2f historically suits a horse who can travel fluidly and avoid energy wastage early — any horse showing signs of pulling hard in the first half-mile should be downgraded significantly given the conditions.

races.name: Fitzdares Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Everatease
runners_data.note: Two consecutive wins on Good ground over 6f and strong recent form (664110) make this a live closer, but Eve Johnson Houghton's 11-day return is fine and Callum Hutchinson must trust that a fast-ground tempo materialises to give this horse's hold-up style any chance in a five-runner race.

runners_data.name: El Lambo
runners_data.note: Won on Firm ground over 6f suggesting the conditions suit, but Rob Hornby will have limited options to work from the back in a field this small — El Lambo's natural style is hold-up but it has been mapped to midfield by necessity, meaning it is likely to race in a compromised position rather than its ideal slot.

runners_data.name: Harry Knows
runners_data.note: The top-rated runner at OR 86 with Oisin Murphy aboard, Harry Knows is the lone front-runner in this field and has finished placed on four of five career starts; wearing a hood, it should stride to the front unchallenged and Murphy can control the race throughout on ground where this horse has shown its best form.

runners_data.name: Keep Kicking On
runners_data.note: Returned a winner last time over this exact 6f-Good combination and Hector Crouch knows the horse, but three weeks off and a hold-up style in a small field mean Keep Kicking On needs Harry Knows to roll along honestly enough to be reeled in late; Clive Cox's quiet 14-day strike rate (1/18) is worth noting.

runners_data.name: This Moment
runners_data.note: A consistent young filly with three runs all at 6f on Good ground, all producing placed efforts, and Billy Loughnane's positive front-foot riding style makes this the most natural challenger to Harry Knows if the prominent position is contested; 42 days off is the main query for George Boughey's charge.

races.paceDynamic: Harry Knows is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with only This Moment as a secondary prominent type to apply any pressure, should stride into an uncontested lead and control tempo from the gates on Good to Firm ground over 6f at Windsor. This Moment will sit just off the early pace, meaning the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching — Harry Knows can dictate a comfortable, sustainable gallop and accelerate when it suits. The hold-up horses Everatease and Keep Kicking On will need that front-runner to set an honest pace to bring their finishing kicks into play, and with just five runners, there is nowhere to hide if the pace is moderate. This shape clearly favours the prominent-to-lead profile: a single pace-setter dictating on fast ground over 6f is a near-ideal scenario for the horse on the front end and those who can latch onto that position early. The field carries more genuine hold-up intent than the map can place at the rear — El Lambo is a true hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map, and Keep Kicking On and Everatease are the horses most naturally suited to those rearward positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Harry Knows Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Harry Knows leads unchallenged from the gates and sets a fair but not punishing tempo.
scenarios.body: Harry Knows, dictated to by Oisin Murphy, controls every yard on Good to Firm ground and quickens away from two furlongs out, never seriously pressured; the hold-up horses simply cannot generate enough momentum against a front-runner who has never had to race hard to get his position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Harry Knows goes too fast in the early stages and the pace becomes genuinely strong.
scenarios.body: A hot early gallop stretches the field and leaves the front two vulnerable inside the final furlong, allowing the hold-up horses to reel them in off a true pace; Everatease and Keep Kicking On, both proven winners over this course and distance combination on similar ground, are best equipped to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: This Moment Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If This Moment tracks Harry Knows at the perfect distance and produces a well-timed challenge at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Billy Loughnane times a cover move to perfection, sitting a length off Harry Knows before angling out and collaring the leader late; This Moment's consistent form figures over 6f on Good ground suggest this is a realistic counter-shape if Harry Knows slightly over-exerts early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: El Lambo Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If the small field breaks slowly and pace collapses entirely, allowing El Lambo to land a blow from a forward position.
scenarios.body: El Lambo's sole win came on Firm ground over 6f and the conditions here are not far removed, but this scenario is materially discounted because El Lambo is a true hold-up type shuffled to midfield on the map and is unlikely to access a favourable position naturally in a five-runner field.

watchPoints.text: Harry Knows wears headgear (hood) — watch for any signs of reluctance or erratic early behaviour at the start, which is the one scenario that could disrupt the expected front-running control.

Keep Kicking On and Everatease both operate as hold-up horses in a five-runner field — if the early tempo is modest, watch whether either jockey elects to push forward early rather than trail in last with no cover.

El Lambo's redistribution from hold-up to midfield on the map is forced by the race shape — watch the early stages to see whether Rob Hornby can negotiate a genuine prominent berth or is pushed back to his natural last position, as this will define whether El Lambo has any realistic chance.

This Moment has not run for 42 days — watch the pre-race market moves and paddock condition closely, as George Boughey's 14-day strike rate (5/24) suggests the yard is live but this filly's freshness on the day is an unknown.

races.name: Join Fitzdares For A Personal Service Ebf Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Major Looktwice
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore stable have a solid record with lightly raced juveniles and Hector Crouch is a capable pilot, but with no racecourse form whatsoever the running style is entirely unknown — could be anything from natural leader to hold-up, making this a genuine wildcard in a chaotic pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Parkers Light
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's runner arrives on moderate form (fifth and eighth in two starts at 6f), and while William Cox is an able claimer, the absence of a win or place and the likelihood of being outgunned for early pace by Real Bullet and Wateera suggests this one may get swallowed up mid-race rather than influencing the finish.

runners_data.name: Real Bullet
runners_data.note: George Boughey's colt is the most credentialled runner in the field, having won his debut over this course and distance in Good ground — Billy Loughnane keeps the ride and the combination looks formidable; the key question is whether a three-way pace battle takes the edge off what looked an electric performance first time out.

runners_data.name: Wateera
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's filly has winning course and distance form and a solid recent run to back it up, giving her solid claims on paper, though 48 days off the track introduces a small fitness caveat; Clifford Lee rides a stable in excellent current form (8 winners from 46 runners in 14 days) and will be looking to use this filly's proven track record aggressively from the front.

runners_data.name: Aksel
runners_data.note: Michael Attwater's debutant arrives completely unexposed with no public form to assess — Seamus Cronin takes the 5lb claim which helps the handicap weight, but the UNKNOWN style tag means there is no reliable basis to map where this horse will race; best treated as a dark horse whose role in the race shape becomes clearer at the stalls.

runners_data.name: Goldtrader
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's runner showed a fading finish flag on debut at 5f in Good ground and steps up to 6f here after 79 days off — if the extra furlong improves him, Kieran Shoemark will have the experience to hold him up off the likely strong pace and hope for a late rattle through tired horses, though the tendency to fade is a genuine concern.

races.paceDynamic: Real Bullet, Parkers Light, and Wateera are all confirmed front-runners in a six-runner field, guaranteeing an honest, pressure-filled gallop from the outset at Windsor's straight six furlongs on Good to Firm ground. Real Bullet brings the strongest recent form (winning debut over this exact course and distance in Good ground), while Wateera has won over this track and trip too, meaning neither will concede the lead cheaply — the pace battle between these three will be genuine and sustained. Parkers Light has less to recommend on form (finishing fifth and eighth), so is likely the weakest of the trio in the speed battle, but their mere presence adds further pressure to the leaders. This race shape firmly favours a hold-up or prominent horse with a strong late kick, as the contested early fractions will drain the front-runners; the profile to back is one who can travel off the pace and motor through tiring rivals in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way battle for the lead burns out the front-runners before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Real Bullet, Wateera, and Parkers Light fight for supremacy through the first three furlongs, leaving them vulnerable to anything coming with a sustained late run; Goldtrader, despite a fading-finish flag, and Major Looktwice or Aksel (unknown styles) could theoretically swoop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Real Bullet Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Real Bullet breaks best and dictates a sustainable tempo, resisting the challenge of Wateera and Parkers Light.
scenarios.body: Having already won over course and distance on identical ground, Real Bullet is the most proven performer here, and Billy Loughnane's experience could see him slot into a workable lead after the initial scrap subsides; if the pace settles rather than boils over, Real Bullet's class edge could see him grind out victory.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Wateera Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Wateera secures the rail and imposes a controlled gallop, rationing stamina better than rivals.
scenarios.body: Wateera has won over course and distance in Good ground and Clifford Lee may look to slot across and dictate from the front, using track knowledge to minimise the pace war; if the fractions are less suicidal than they could be, Wateera's proven course form gives her a genuine chance to outstay the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutants Steal It
scenarios.trigger: If Major Looktwice or Aksel, both unknown quantities on debut, are naturally prominent and hit the line full of running while the known front-runners tie each other up.
scenarios.body: Two lightly raced, unraced runners with unknown styles could be anything — if either is a natural hold-up type with raw ability, the carnage among the front-runners sets up a perfect late-arriving winner; George Boughey and Ed Walker respectively have the handler quality to produce a sharp debutant, but this is the most speculative shape given the total absence of form data.

watchPoints.text: Real Bullet, Wateera, and Parkers Light all broke keenly in previous runs — watch the first two furlongs for a genuine speed duel that could fatally compromise all three front-runners before halfway.

Goldtrader's 79-day absence combined with a fading-finish profile at 5f means there is real doubt about whether the extra furlong and the time off track combine positively or produce another empty display late on.

Major Looktwice and Aksel are both first-time starters with entirely unknown running styles — either could emerge from the pack as a natural hold-up type perfectly suited to picking off the exhausted pace-setters, making them impossible to dismiss despite the absence of any form.

K.R. Burke's trainer strike rate of 8/46 over the past 14 days is the strongest in this field — Wateera represents a live contender from a stable firing, and Clifford Lee's booking for a course-and-distance winner warrants respect.

Windsor's straight six favours horses who can be produced late with one clean run through the field — any scrimmaging for position early among the three front-runners could create gaps that even modest closers exploit in the final 100 yards.

races.name: Fitzdares Sprint Series Final Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Diligently
runners_data.note: Clive Cox handler has strong 14-day numbers but this is a horse whose natural race is from the back — with the rear already packed, Billy Loughnane will likely find himself racing a position or two ahead of where Diligently wants to be, and the STYLE_FIT tag is a legitimate concern in this shape.

runners_data.name: Justcallmepete
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with two wins from six Good-ground starts at 6f and a tongue tie fitted; Dougie Costello should push for a prominent pitch from the draw and his recent 5f run at Goodwood suggests fitness is fine heading into this final.

runners_data.name: Dream Composer
runners_data.note: Veteran campaigner who has won twice on Good at 5f but whose true preference is to close from the rear — the field's depth of hold-up types means Tony Carroll's charge will likely race closer than ideal, and the STYLE_FIT discount is applicable in a race this well-populated at the back.

runners_data.name: Purest Time
runners_data.note: Ian Williams runner who won a 6f Good contest recently but has been wayward in form since; Edward Greatrex picks up the ride and the horse's natural closing style is squeezed by redistribution, making it harder to access the position that yielded that win.

runners_data.name: Star Chorus
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby takes the ride on a 4yo who wears hood and has been running from the rear without reward in recent outings — no wins in the last five on sim-going, and being forced forward of natural position in a 16-runner sprint is unlikely to unlock improvement.

runners_data.name: Baldomero
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 8yo carries a visor and has placed twice on Good ground over today's course and distance, but his hold-up approach is compromised by redistribution into midfield; Harry Davies will struggle to find the daylight this horse needs late.

runners_data.name: Badri
runners_data.note: The form anchor of the race — four wins from five on Good ground over sprint trips, including back-to-back 6f wins, and Oisin Murphy takes over in what is a clear riding booking for the favourite; the lone front-runner role suits perfectly and his OR=99 mark reflects a horse in the form of his life.

runners_data.name: King Of Light
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams 4yo who won a 6f Good contest earlier in his recent form and has Marco Ghiani booked; prominent style fits this race shape well and a return to Good ground after a couple of disappointing efforts on faster should help his cause.

runners_data.name: Trefor
runners_data.note: Charles Hills runner who has a solid record of four wins at prominent pace but whose recent figures are modest — a sequence of 0-0400 is not encouraging and the sim-going count of 14 runs without recent success signals he needs everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Indian Run
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 5yo who won a 6f Good handicap and finished second to a useful rival on the same ground recently; Ryan Sexton takes the ride and this is a horse with the strongest case among the genuine hold-up types who are not redistibuted — his form at 6f on Good is legitimate.

runners_data.name: Another Abbot
runners_data.note: William Haggas 4yo wearing a tongue tie and carrying Tom Marquand — two wins and multiple places at 6f on Good ground make the profile solid; the concern is whether 16 runners at 6f leaves sufficient room for a genuine closer to deliver, but Marquand's race-reading ability is an asset.

runners_data.name: Desert Cop
runners_data.note: George Baker's 6yo with blinkers, who won a 6f Good contest in his last victory and has been placed four times on sim-going; Benoit de la Sayette partners and the horse's form is solid enough, though 20-length beaten efforts in big fields hint at the difficulty of his closing style in a race like this.

runners_data.name: Sudden Flight
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes 4yo who has hit the board in four of his last five at 6f and is fitted with blinkers; a prominent style that suits the shape, and while he has yet to win, his consistent placing record on Good ground at this trip marks him as a natural framing horse in Scenario A.

runners_data.name: Rosario
runners_data.note: Roger Teal 5yo whose recent form has been at 5f rather than today's 6f — the step back up in trip introduces some uncertainty; Hector Crouch is an able claimer but the horse's win record and recent placings have all come at the minimum sprint distance.

runners_data.name: Cindy Lou Who
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's 4yo has William Carson in the saddle and a prominent style that will push for position from the jump; a winless record on Good ground over 6f (form reading 9-2-9-0) is a concern, and three runners from the same yard may create slight logistical complications.

runners_data.name: Uncle Don
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell 4yo who has been off for 56 days — the longest absence in the field — and while two second-place efforts on Good ground are on his record, the layoff and Clifford Lee's booking are neutral signals rather than positives heading into a competitive 16-runner sprint finale.

races.paceDynamic: Badri is the confirmed front-runner here and, with Oisin Murphy in the saddle, will be allowed to stride on and control matters from the front at a pace he dictates — Good to Firm ground at Windsor suits his recent winning sequence perfectly. King Of Light, Trefor, Justcallmepete, Sudden Flight and Cindy Lou Who will all press for prominent positions early, creating genuine pressure behind the leader even if Badri himself is not directly challenged for the lead. The field carries substantially more pace than the map can accommodate — Diligently, Purest Time, Dream Composer, Star Chorus and Baldomero are all true hold-up horses redistibuted into midfield slots because the rear of the field is already full; they are unlikely to access their natural deep-closing position and their effectiveness late is compromised. This race shape — a single leader controlling a strong pace with a cluttered midfield of displaced closers — decisively favours horses that can race prominently off the front end and sustain their effort, or genuine hold-up performers with enough room to weave through; a sustainable but honest pace means truly prominent types tracking Badri are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Badri Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Badri dictates a genuine but manageable pace and the prominent chasers sustain their challenge into the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Badri sets a fair gallop on fast ground that suits his recent dominance, and horses immediately tracking him — King Of Light, Sudden Flight, Trefor — have the clearest run through to challenge; the pace is honest enough to expose hold-up types stuck in a congested midfield.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If Badri misjudges or is pushed and the pace turns messy, allowing genuine hold-up horses to arrive late.
scenarios.body: A falsely run or bunched race would give Indian Run, Another Abbot and Desert Cop — true hold-up performers with solid recent form — the late momentum to pick off tiring leaders; their sim-going records and finishing form make them the natural beneficiaries of any pace collapse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge Through Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field and create a gap through the centre for runners tracking the leaders at mid-division.
scenarios.body: Horses like Indian Run and Desert Cop, with strong course-and-distance profiles and jockeys capable of threading through traffic, could exploit a well-strung field; the key is enough separation in the pack to avoid the redistribution problem that handicaps the deeper closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Badri is essentially unchallenged early and turns the race into a procession, with his rivals unable to close the gap.
scenarios.body: Given Badri's four wins from five on Good ground at sprint trips and Murphy's ability to judge pace perfectly, a wire-to-wire performance is plausible if the prominent chasers fail to maintain their position or make tactical errors early; the weight he carries at OR=99 is the sole check on this outcome.

watchPoints.text: Badri's early jumping and positioning will set the entire race tempo — if Murphy eases him out alone, the prominent chasers (King Of Light, Sudden Flight, Trefor) must decide immediately whether to commit or drop off, and that decision in the first furlong shapes every scenario.

The redistribution cluster of Diligently, Dream Composer, Purest Time, Star Chorus and Baldomero creates a congested mid-pack — watch for traffic problems and interference between the 3f and 1f markers as these displaced hold-up types fail to find their natural racing room.

Indian Run and Another Abbot are the two genuine hold-up performers NOT flagged as redistributed; if either gets a clear run on the stands rail or through the centre from the 2f pole, they represent the most credible late threats to Badri's dominance.

Tony Carroll saddles three runners (Justcallmepete, Dream Composer, Cindy Lou Who) — watch which one receives the most significant market move pre-race as a guide to stable confidence, and note whether the three jockey bookings suggest any inter-stable instructions.

Going is Good to Firm for this race despite the card heading showing Good — Badri's recent wins have come on Good ground and the upgrade to faster conditions is worth monitoring, particularly for any horse whose headgear or style note references soft-ground form as their best.

races.name: Fitzdares Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Gift Box
runners_data.note: Unraced and unknown in terms of running style, top-weight at 128lbs for Laura Mongan with William Carson booked — the unknown factor here is considerable but the OR=120 ceiling hints connections are hopeful she is well ahead of any initial rating.

runners_data.name: Sterling Fortune
runners_data.note: Best form has come on softer ground (a third at Goodwood) and her hold-up style is genuinely compromised in this shape — Good to Firm at Windsor with only one confirmed front-runner means she will find little injection of pace to aim at late on.

runners_data.name: Dayna
runners_data.note: The only confirmed pace-setter in the race, she has posted two fifth-place finishes at 7f and 8f on Good ground but the key asset here is that nobody will dispute her lead, giving Clifford Lee total control of tempo; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects she is set to race more actively than her profile ideally suits.

runners_data.name: Princess Honey Bee
runners_data.note: Five career runs show a consistent placed record on Good and Good to Firm, and her 334-22 string demonstrates she handles this surface well — she is a natural hold-up filly whose best chance comes if she can push forward from her redistributed midfield slot and race closer than usual.

runners_data.name: Moonswept
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and a complete unknown quantity like Gift Box, but Daniel and Claire Kubler send her out with Ebrahim Nader, a combination worth noting on a quick surface; no historical data means this is a blind entry whose true ability is entirely concealed.

runners_data.name: Mystic Music
runners_data.note: A long 127-day absence for Andrew Balding is the headline concern, and her two runs came over 12f and 8f on the all-weather — stepping back to 1m on turf in Good to Firm conditions is a significant shift in parameters for a filly returning from a four-month break.

runners_data.name: Somethingintheair
runners_data.note: Trained by J S Moore with J F Egan up, she has a best run of third over 8f on Good ground at Goodwood which gives her the most relevant going profile of the displaced hold-up types, though racing out of her natural late role on a non-searching tempo is a clear handicap.

runners_data.name: Thunder Goddess
runners_data.note: Second Balding runner alongside Mystic Music, she is absent for 140 days with form only on the all-weather over 8f and 10f — the drop in trip, the turf surface, and the lengthy break all combine to make her current readiness difficult to assess with confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Dayna is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine pressing rival, she is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop on Good to Firm ground around Windsor's flat mile. That controlled tempo means the pace is honest but not truly searching, which keeps the race together rather than stringing it out early. Mystic Music and Thunder Goddess are the only true hold-up types not displaced by the redistribution, meaning any late surge depends on a field that genuinely gaps in the final two furlongs. The race shape strongly favours horses who can sit just off Dayna's shoulder in the prominent-to-midfield berth and deliver a smooth, progressive challenge — pure closers face a less certain proposition here given the pace is unlikely to be truly end-to-end. Note that this field contains more hold-up and prominent types than the map can naturally accommodate: Princess Honey Bee, Sterling Fortune, and Somethingintheair are genuine hold-up horses shuffled into midfield slots on the map, with Dayna and any lightly-raced unexposed types most likely to actually dictate terms at the business end.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dayna Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Dayna leads unchallenged at a steady-to-moderate clip and the race is decided by a sustained challenge from just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Dayna sets a comfortable fractions-controlled gallop and the winner emerges from the prominent group tracking her into the straight, where Good to Firm ground rewards a horse travelling smoothly rather than finishing from deep. Horses positioned second or third through the race have the shortest route to the line and avoid the traffic risks that crowd the midfield.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Unexposed Types Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly-raced OR=120 debutantes or returning fillies produces a performance beyond their limited exposed form.
scenarios.body: Gift Box or Moonswept, both unraced or lightly tried and carrying top weight off an OR ceiling, could be significantly ahead of their bare ratings and produce a decisive, visually impressive effort that the established form lines never flagged.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely brisk enough to compress the field and allow true hold-up runners to reel in a tiring leader in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Mystic Music or Thunder Goddess, both trained by Andrew Balding and racing on a firmer surface over a trip that may suit better than their all-weather form suggests, find a late gap if the early pace has been more taxing than it appeared.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Dash Home
scenarios.trigger: If Dayna goes off too fast for her own fitness level and the race degenerates into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: With Dayna having run just twice and showing only modest form at shorter, a misjudged effort could see her weakening sharply, turning the contest into a sprint that benefits the speediest finisher regardless of earlier position.

watchPoints.text: Dayna sets a pace that could be either too slow or too fast for her own fitness — monitor her early fractions closely because her ability to control tempo dictates the shape of the entire race.

Gift Box and Moonswept are both unknown quantities whose OR=120 ceilings could be dramatically understating their ability — if either shows early professional behaviour in the preliminaries, treat them as serious threats regardless of absent form.

Princess Honey Bee has the most consistent form record in the field on this going, but she must race out of her natural style in a limited-pace scenario — watch whether Billy Loughnane pushes her forward aggressively from the start rather than dropping her in as usual.

Both Andrew Balding runners (Mystic Music and Thunder Goddess) carry significant fitness questions after lengthy absences — if either moves fluently through the race without the expected greenness, their trainer's powerful 8/54 T14 strike rate suggests they are ready to run well.

races.name: Listen To Track Radio Live Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Fizzy Bear
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo for George Baker, absent 82 days which is a significant concern; good-ground form is limited (0 wins, 0 places on similar going) and a hold-up style leaves her entirely dependent on pace and a clean passage in what will be a congested finish.

runners_data.name: My Old Mate
runners_data.note: Won over course and distance in good-ground conditions and has shown early pace before — the Billy Loughnane booking is notable — but this is a horse whose natural instinct is to come from behind, and the pace-making role is an artificial one that will test its finishing resolution; tagged as fading in the finish which compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Ingemar
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's charge ran 12 days ago and arrives fresh enough; its true nature is a hold-up runner but the map places it in midfield given the overcrowded rear — at 8f on good ground it has placed before and the headgear (hood) may sharpen early concentration, though the crowded finish is a lottery for a horse needing to come from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Torbados
runners_data.note: Charles Hills-trained, blinkered, and has placed on similar going (4th, 5th in recent starts); steps up from 6-7f to a mile which is a potential trip concern, though the form string shows consistency without ever winning — Rob Hornby is a strong booking but the horse needs to prove a mile suits.

runners_data.name: Twilight Baby
runners_data.note: Gay Kelleway has had a quiet recent trainer strike rate (0 from 4 over 14 days) and Tom Marquand partners this filly who has only one top-3 finish in three starts; she fades in finishes according to her tag, and a hold-up style crammed into midfield on a day when closers are disadvantaged by modest pace is not an ideal combination.

runners_data.name: Landslide
runners_data.note: Oliver Cole's 3yo has headgear on (hood) and a trainer firing at a reasonable 3/13 strike rate over 14 days; its natural instinct is to race from the rear, and recent form (5th, 8th, 6th, 10th) on good ground makes it hard to be enthusiastic about its prospects in a race where hold-up runners are already squeezed.

runners_data.name: Karisma's Angel
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly carries a strong jockey booking in Kieran Shoemark, and her best run (3rd at 7f on good ground) suggests some ability — she has been 2nd on standard ground and has course-relevant form, but her true hold-up style is displaced into midfield and she needs the straight to open up quickly for her to arrive with her best effort.

runners_data.name: Creciente
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on a horse that has won and placed prolifically on good ground (11 from 12 placings on similar going), making this the standout good-ground performer in the race; Rod Millman sends him out 9 days after his last run and a step up from 7f to 1m looks potentially positive given his profile, though the true hold-up nature pushed into midfield means he needs a clean run.

runners_data.name: Neat And Tidy
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's filly is unplaced in five of her last five starts and consistently finishes in the 5th-to-11th range on standard ground; Finley Marsh takes over in the saddle and a step up to 1m is unexplored territory — nothing in the form recommends her strongly for this race shape.

runners_data.name: Bennyworth
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's 3yo has good-ground experience at 8f with a pair of 4th-place finishes at the trip, and Tyler Heard partners a horse that at least stays the distance; rated lowest in the field at OR 52, its only realistic route to involvement is a traffic-chaos scenario where better-rated rivals block themselves in the straight.

runners_data.name: Mr Jeffrey
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated horse alongside the most modest form string in the race (0787 recently), and tagged as fading in finishes; Ashley Lewis claims 3lb but the horse has not threatened a top-3 finish and its hold-up style mapping to midfield in a modest-paced race does it no favours whatsoever.

races.paceDynamic: My Old Mate is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this race, redistributed to the front because no other horse is a natural leader — in reality a hold-up type being asked to do a job that does not come naturally, meaning the early tempo is likely to be modest and controllable rather than truly pressured. With one horse setting a sustainable, uncontested gallop over Windsor's flat mile, the pace map produces a single-file, strung-out shape where the leader dictates terms and a genuine sprint for home develops in the straight. This race shape historically favours horses that can travel prominently or in the first half of the field and quicken, rather than deep closers who need a true end-to-end gallop to get into it. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Ingemar, Twilight Baby, Landslide, Karisma's Angel, Creciente, Neat And Tidy, Bennyworth and Mr Jeffrey are all genuine back-of-the-field types, meaning most of them will be racing against their natural instincts and will crowd each other in the closing stages; the runners most likely to actually secure a forward position are My Old Mate on the lead and any of the bolder-jumping hold-up types who break quickly from the gate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Tempo, Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If My Old Mate settles comfortably on a modest, uncontested lead and controls the race from the front without being challenged for position.
scenarios.body: My Old Mate bowls along at a steady clip, the field strings out behind in a disorganised bunch, and the race becomes a sprint for home over the final two furlongs — the leader's natural hold-up ability means it does not fade as badly as it might since the pace is self-regulated. Horses capable of travelling in the first half of the field and producing a sharp turn of foot in the straight benefit most; deep closers who need a strong pace to close into are left without the fuel to mow down a leader who has had a comfortable time of it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Pace Compression, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the steady gallop compresses the field so tightly that multiple hold-up horses arrive simultaneously at the two-furlong pole with a clear run.
scenarios.body: A bunched field turns for home in a wall of horses, and those who find daylight earliest in the straight get the decisive advantage; Creciente's strong good-ground form and Oisin Murphy's positional awareness in these compressed finishes make that pairing particularly dangerous. The crowded hold-up division means traffic is the defining factor, and the horse that threads through first rather than the one with the most raw ability wins.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If My Old Mate, racing out of its natural role, nonetheless finds the steady tempo so comfortable that rivals simply cannot sustain a challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: The modest gallop asks no serious questions of the leader until it is too late for the hold-up pack to close the gap from deep positions, and My Old Mate, benefiting from the race it has stolen rather than earned, holds on grimly. Horses finishing with any sort of proximity — those who tracked within three lengths — are the main dangers, but the outcome is sealed by the lack of a credible mid-race challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Finish, Outsider Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded hold-up division produces severe interference and multiple market leaders are impeded, allowing a lower-rated runner to slip through unnoticed.
scenarios.body: With eight genuine hold-up types all hunting clear ground simultaneously in the final two furlongs at Windsor, a horse that draws a clean lane along the rail or the wide outside can steal the race from a field that is blocking itself. Bennyworth or Fizzy Bear, both operating below market expectation, could exploit the traffic chaos if they inherit a clean passage that the better-fancied horses cannot find.

watchPoints.text: My Old Mate is being asked to lead from the front against its natural instincts — watch for signs of it drifting or weakening sharply once headed in the straight, which could trigger a rapid unravelling of the entire race shape.

Creciente arrives just 9 days after its last run with Oisin Murphy in the saddle and boasts by far the strongest good-ground win rate in the field — if it gets a clean passage from a midfield position it has the profile to finish fastest of all.

The overcrowded hold-up division — eight genuine rear-runners attempting to find clear ground simultaneously at Windsor's straight — creates a high risk of significant traffic interference in the final two furlongs; horses drawn widest may benefit most.

Torbados wears blinkers and steps up in trip from 6-7f to a mile for the first time — monitor whether Charles Hills has deliberately targeted this trip or whether it is a speculative entry, as the trip question materially changes how to assess its chance.

Karisma's Angel and Ingemar both have decent recent placings on good ground at 7-8f and carry strong jockey bookings (Shoemark, Leavy) — in the compressed-finish scenario either could produce a late surge if they inherit an unobstructed run along the rail.
